academicJudgment.claim: The confirmed population-health, behavioural, lifespan and research-methods core supports a meaningful broader UCR programme in population health, behaviour and social policy; the unverified final-year research/professional culmination is outside this comparison.
academicJudgment.basis: Actual epidemiological designs/determinants/intervention project, biopsychosocial health/behaviour, lifespan development, quantitative/qualitative/evidence-synthesis work and specific policy/equity contributions establish meaningful sustained subject responsiveness. Biological mechanisms support population outcomes but are not substituted for health systems.
academicJudgment.strongestObjection: A general biomedical/psychology programme would not suffice. Replaced an additional organ-pathophysiology course and generic civil-society seminar with actual public-policy analysis and organisational psychology. Dedicated healthcare systems and implementation remain gaps, but confirmed health-determinant/behaviour/methods substance is directly sustained rather than supplied only through contextual breadth.
